name: Thief's Journal
text:
[This looks like a journal of the thief who tried to rob the tomb. It has many personal entries, but only some bits that may be important to you.]
...I’ve got a very weird job offer today. A man named Elvas Savel wants me to make a mess in a tomb belonging to his own family and throw some Hlaalu stuff around. Make it look like tomb robbers, he said. I think that he plans to link the “robbery” to some Hlaalu noble from Vivec. Hah. I can make that convincing, for sure. Happy to take all the loot from the tomb.
Inter Fendrath Aran
I picked up the remains of Fendrath Aran. I should deliver them to the Aran Ancestral Tomb, northwest of Mababi.
The tomb has been defiled by daedra. I'll need to purge it of the mad dead and interlopers before I can inter Fendrath's remains.
The Aran tomb is now at peace once again.
I interred Fendrath Aran in the tomb.
I received payment from the Keepers.
I failed to deliver the remains.
Arethan Tomb Purification
I was asked to purge the Arethan Tomb of Daedra and corrupted tomb guardians.
I performed the purification duty in the Arethan Tomb and made my report to the Keepers.
Inter Seryndil Vandus
I picked up the remains of Seryndil Vandus from Keerin Meille. I should deliver them to the Vandus Ancestral Tomb, near Lake Nabia.
I interred Seryndil Vandus in the tomb.
I reported back to Keerin.
I failed to deliver the remains.
Savel Investigation
I was asked to investigate reports of theft at the Savel Ancestral Tomb.
Elvas Savel is working with Baren Alen.
I struck a deal between Baren Alen and Elvas Savel.
Elvas Savel rewarded me.
I struck a deal with Baren Alen, to ruin Elvas Savel.
I made my report to the Keepers. I got Elvas Savel to withdraw his claims.
I made my report to the Keepers. I got Elvas Savel to withdraw his claims.
I made my report to the Keepers.
I made my report the Keepers. Elvas Savel is dead.
Daedric Detective
Find the stone that was stolen from the Beran Tomb.
Giron Manas denies ever having been to the Beran Ancestral Tomb.

I confronted Giron Manas with the bloodied journal I found in Beran Ancestral Tomb. He confessed to guiding the high elf into the tomb and taking an obsidian orb that was hidden there. He sold the orb in town.
Fadase Selvayn bought the orb, and said he later sold it to Barnand Erelie.
Barnand hid the orb outside the tower in a mucksponge.
I found the mucksponge, but there was no orb.
Barnand suggested that the Telvanni must have stolen the orb.
I've recovered the orb from Darvasa Vedas.
I handed the orb over to D'lgotha.
I handed the orb over to Vep'ious'andra.
I handed orb over to the Keepers.
I told the Keepers that I couldn't find the source of the Daedric infestation.
Permission to Audit
Firsylla has asked me to secure permission from Mistress Therana in Tel Branora so the Keepers of the Dead can perform an official audit of the ancestral tombs there.
Therana has agreed to allow an audit if I kill Dalen.
Therana has agreed to allow an audit if I bring her 33 large kwama eggs and 22 small kwama eggs.
Therana wants an egg before she will grant the Keepers access to the tombs.
Therana has agreed to allow the tombs to be audited.
Mistress Therana is dead. There's no need to get her permission.
I told Firsylla that we have permission to audit the tombs.
Audit Arano Tomb
I need to conduct an audit of Arano Ancestral Tomb, near Tel Branora.
Vep’ious’andra, a Seducer occupying the tomb, offered me a saber if I kill her rival and retrieve an orb that was stolen from her. She also alluded to other rewards.
I killed the Seducer and made my report to Firsylla.
I made my report to Firsylla, but omitted the Seducer.
Audit Beran Tomb
I need to conduct an audit of Beran Ancestral Tomb, near Tel Branora.
I made my report to Firsylla.
Meet the Boss
Keerin Meille has arranged a meeting with me and his other employer. I'll need to follow the tunnel in the Molag Mar Underworks to deliver some stolen remains.
I told Firsylla about Keerin's misappropriation, and returned the stolen remains to her.
I met D'lgotha, a Sload necromancer. He has work for me.
I followed the tunnel as Keerin instructed me and met D'lgotha, a Sload necromancer. He has work for me.
Helan Tomb Investigation
I agreed to investigate eerie voices in Helan Ancestral Tomb.
I killed the necromancer and made my report to Ondar.
Sewer Snoop
I agreed to deal with Buoyant Armiger snooping around in the Molag Mar underworks.
I convinced the Buoyant Armiger to leave.
I reported that the Buoyant Armiger has ended their investigation.
I reported that I killed the Buoyant Armiger.
Velas Ancestral Testimony
I was asked to investigate Velas Ancestral Tomb and to uncover what happened to a missing Ordinator who was sent to the area.
I collected ancestral testimony from the ghost in Velas Ancestral Tomb and learned the truth about Goron Velas. Apparently, he is now a lich.
I was tricked by Taluri Velas’ ghost in Velas Ancestral Tomb. I still need to make my report to the Keepers.
I made my report to Firsylla.
Arethan Family Revenge

I met the ghost of Torosi Arethan in the Arethan Tomb. She said she was trapped in the tomb with “pests” due to the schemes of her own family. She wants to imprison Elo Arethan and asked me to expose his involvement in a smuggling ring to Ordinators in Vivec.
I contacted Elo Arethan. He proposed a deal. He wants me to bring him the soul of Torosi Arethan in return for a book from his collection and Telvanni bug musk.
I revealed Elo Arethan’s schemes.
I brought a soul gem with Torosi Arethan’s soul to Elo Arethan.
Retheran Apology
I was asked to apologize to Fonas Retheran on behalf of the Keepers of the Dead for misplacing the remains of her close relative and negotiate recompense, should she demand it.

Fonas Retheran told me that she would lower her demand for recompense if I returned her lost family relic. She said that it’s a war axe and that Edwinna Elbert of the Mages Guild in Ald’ruhn has it now.
Fonas Retheran demanded a formal apology and 8000 gold as recompense.
I managed to convince Fonas Retheran to accept a formal apology and 1000 gold as recompense.
Firsylla was surprised to learn of Fonas Retheran’s death.
Hlervu Tomb Hauntings
I was asked to investigate Hlervu Tomb as the potential source of recent hauntings.

I went to Hlervu Tomb and met a woman there who called herself Cinia Carrus. Apparently, she is responsible for the hauntings. She is looking for the staff of the lich Goron Velas. She said she would stop the hauntings for now, but wants me to bring her the staff.
I made my report about Hlervu Tomb hauntings to the Keepers.
Rolasa Deleth's Case
I was asked to negotiate with Elislas, the father of Rolasa Deleth, a Dunmer who was wounded while performing her duties as the messenger. Elislas is staying in Pilgrim’s Rest.
I told Elislas that the Keepers would not provide any additional compensation.
I told Elislas that the Keepers would provide some additional compensation.
I told Elislas that the Keepers would provide substantial additional compensation.
I made my report to the Keepers about Rolasa Deleth's case.
I informed the Keepers about Elislas' death.
More disruptions? I had hoped to conduct my experiments in this corner of the tower in some peace. What do you want?

text: What do you want? You know you’ve been expelled.
%PCRank. Do you have anything to report?

Oh, hello. Are you here to join the Keepers of the Dead? Then you will need to talk with Firsylla Dulo. Only she can admit you. We’re still reeling from all the trial disruptions, so don’t be surprised if some things seem chaotic.
Greetings, %PCRank. What can I do for you?
What do you want?
Are you here to help? If you want to join the Keepers, Firsylla Dulo handles the recruitment.
You’re a traitor. I don’t like talking to traitors.
Yes, %PCRank? What do you need?

Hmm? I’m sorry deary, but St. Veloth’s Hostel is full. So many people bustling around a small space. I much prefer a quieter working environment, but there’s too much to do and not enough room to do it in.
Oh, do I know you? You’re very familiar. No wait, don’t tell me. Yves? No… %PCName! Yes, how can I help you, little one?
Oh, young blood! Welcome to the Keepers of the Dead, %PCName. I’m Nance Bero, it’s a pleasure to meet you.
Ah, %PCName! I was told you were coming down here to help me out. Thanks for the assistance; it’s a lot of work pushing pots around this island and my back is screaming at me. Ready to get to work?
%PCName! Just who I wanted to see. How have you been?
Oh, hello! I’m down here taking a break from pushing pots all over this island. The hostel upstairs has been commandeered by the Keepers of the Dead, so this is the only decent tavern in town.
I’ll be leaving shortly.
Yes, %PCRace? Do you plan on staying here for long? I wish I didn’t have to come to this place at all.

I’m Nance Bero, the Archivist for the Keepers here in Molag Mar. I must admit I was torn on taking the assignment here, but my late great-great-great third uncle, Eno Bero, convinced me to leave Necrom one last time and see the world. Did you know he served on a military ship against the Camoran Usurper’s legions? Really quite remarkable. I’ve actually never set foot in Vvardenfell before, but I’ve catalogued most of the tombs here from field reports that were sent to my office in Necrom. I don’t think I could stomach another blanched kwama egg. I have a sensitive constitution, you see.

Did my red hair give it away? Yes, I’m Shinathi. It’s not typical for my people to work so closely with the Temple, but I moved to Narsis when I was a child and they were so kind to me. I joined the Temple, and then eventually found my way to Necrom with the Keepers. Nance Bero has been a wonderful mentor, and I’m fortunate that Keerin Meille could join me here.

Some smugglers tunneled into the waterworks and have been using the area to move illicit goods. For your own safety, please vacate.

I’m investigating reports of increased activity down here.
You will regret this!
There are much drier places to think, but it has been relatively crowded in Molag Mar lately. Have you noticed anyone else down here?
Do you take me for a fool, outlander?
Fair enough. Everyone has to eat, even if they need to stoop to eating sewer fish. Have you noticed anyone else down here?
I have trouble believing that a well-off outlander would spend time in the underworks looking for fish.
Corprus monsters here, so close to the Armigers Stronghold? Don’t be ridiculous.

text: It’s a well-positioned fortress. Might not have much in terms of services, but it’s sufficient for pilgrims and warriors who come here. If you need combat training, make sure to visit the Armigers Stronghold. I’ve worked with them before. They know how to handle the blade.

Kill them with fire. Well, it would be better to expose them to the sun, but they know that, so they won’t let you. Fire usually solves the trick and it gives them no choice. Even the ones which were once Dunmer don’t seem to handle fire that well and die in agony, although much slower. It’s all they deserve. Monsters. When fighting vampires, it’s also good to have some means of magicka protection. Many of these creatures use dangerous spells.
Go help out Feldrelo Sadri at the Balmora Temple. She's fallen behind on ash interments.
I don't have anything you can help me with right now.

When you see them, it means the job is hard. Well, maybe not the scamps. Everything else can be pretty mean. A clannfear will sense you from miles away, so don’t rely on stealth. An ogrim can kill you quickly if it gets close, so don’t let it. Flame and frost atronachs have predictable weaknesses to the opposing elements, so use that to your advantage. Don’t get too confident, though. Their magicka reflection abilities can cause you great harm, or even your death. That goes for most Daedric minions, actually. Never use a spell which will instantly kill you if reflected, as it will simply be your last one. And don’t hesitate to use Almsivi Intervention if you get in too much trouble. Yes, it may not be the most heroic act, but it will keep you alive.

Your first task shouldn’t be hard. I won’t be handling it, though. Talk with Keerin Meille. He is in Pilgrim’s Rest, here in Molag Mar. An outlander like you. He’s been doing quite a lot of work for us recently, so I think he deserves a short break. You can take over. And if you need additional information about our current predicament, talk to Ondar Selas.
There is something that Ondar needs done. Talk with him about the details.
Ondar has more work for you. Check with him.

Your work in Helan Ancestral Tomb was impressive, %PCName. You can clearly handle yourself. I want to send you a bit farther away this time, though. You’ll collect ancestral testimony in Velas Ancestral Tomb.
I’ve received a report of Daedra and corrupted tomb guardians in the Arethan Tomb.
I want you to go to the Ghostgate and apologize to Retheran in the name of our Order.
There’ve been several reports about hauntings recently. Reports I received indicate that they may have their source in the Hlervu Tomb.
The ancestral tombs near Tel Branora haven't been assessed for hundreds of years. I need you to get permission to audit the tombs from Mistress Therana.
I need you to conduct an audit of the Arano and Beran tombs near Tel Branora.
I don't have anything new for you right now.
All you need to do is inter remains at Vandus Tomb.
I don’t have anything else ready for you yet, %PCName. Why don’t you take a break and relax for a while?

Good that you are here. I think that I have an assignment well-suited to your abilities. There is an ancestral tomb belonging to the Savel family. It lies east of Molag Mar. If you need detailed directions, I’m sure that Nance Bero will assist you. I want you to go to that tomb and investigate weird reports we’ve received.
I need you to verify the audit of the Helan Tomb.
%PCRank, there is something I want you to help me with. It concerns Rolasa Deleth’s case.
It’s southeast of the island. Giron knows the area well if you need help finding it.
It’s southeast of the island. Giron knows the area well if you need help finding it.
I sold the orb in town. Please, don't tell the guards. I have nothing.

Yes, I went in there. I know it’s not right, but the fishing hasn’t been good this season. I needed money or I’d starve. A man came by asking around for a guide to lead him through the tomb, and I told him I could do it. One of the worst jobs I’ve ever taken in my life. We snuck into the back of the tomb, past a horde of daedra, and then he dug an obsidian orb out of the ash pit.

The daedra noticed us, and in the commotion I ran for my life. It was only at the door of my own home that I realized the orb had somehow made its way into my pocket.

I sold the accursed orb in town. It fetched me enough for a sack of saltrice, and I was happy to be rid of it.

I’m sure one of the fishermen down near the docks can show you the way.
It’s along the shore somewhere. Ask down by the docks and stop bothering me.
I want you to track down this "stone" in Tel Branora, and bring it back to me. I have a suspicion that it's deeply involved in these tomb defilements.
Thank you for tracking down this obsidian orb, %PCName. You have my gratitude.

The preliminary audit is simple. Just conduct a cursory walk through all parts of the tomb. Note any hazards that are present, or if the tomb has been robbed or desecrated. Purge the tomb of any mad undead or daedra that might be present.

The increased daedric presence and this journal put me at unease. Thank you for bringing this to my attention. I want you to track down this "stone" mentioned in the journal, and bring it back to me. I have a suspicion that it's deeply involved in these tomb defilements.
It’s not unheard-of for daedra to infest tombs, but Golden Saints doing so are exceedingly rare. There must be additional clues in the Beran tomb to explain its presence.
This journal is disturbing. A sload in Vvardenfell that is taking interest in the ancestral tombs here needs to be dealt with. Finish clearing the tomb, and report back to me.
Go audit the Beran Ancestral Tomb near Tel Branora.
The Beran Ancestral Tomb is near Tel Branora, along the eastern coast. It's really quite a marvelous construction, from what I can gather.
I bought the trinket from Giron. I thought it would make a nice paperweight if it didn’t sell, but Barnand took it off my hands the very next day. Made a tidy little profit.
I don’t make a habit out of sharing information about my customers’ purchases with strangers.

The orb has some sort of Daedric enchantment on it. My skill in identifying it further is lacking, so I had hoped to send it off to the Mages Guild in Vivec when I concluded my business here. I didn’t want it under my bedroll or Therana’s minions to find it, so I hid it inside a mucksponge outside the tower.
I’m sorry, but I don’t know what you’re talking about.
The orb is missing? Those Telvanni must have noted my suspicious behavior and retraced my steps. How foolish of me! Listen, you can have the orb so long as you keep it out of their hands.
A deal? That could work. There’s a Dark Seducer holed up in a tomb near here. Bring me her soul, and the orb is yours.
You fool!

text: Why are you asking me, outlander? I don’t know where you can get one. Or why you would want one.
I'll send the orb to Necrom for further study, after Ondar is done with it.
I was starting to rely on your abilities, %PCRank. It's unfortunate you were unable to retrieve the artifact.
I don't know what this orb is, but it seems to be at the center of the tomb defilement near Tel Branora. Find it.
This is Tel Branora, %PCName. Everything is suspicious.
Check with Darvasa. She runs security here.
Maybe you’d have better luck asking in the Tower Guardpost? It’s their job to look for such things.
Other than an outlander shoving their nose into other people’s business? No, nothing comes to mind.

Yes. That. To think that Saint Delyn’s Doctrine had to be invoked, and so soon… But I’m sure you know about it. Your colleagues like to keep things interesting, after all. So many challenges issued in a day. I suppose that was to be expected from members of your Great House. But I don’t want to be unfair. The disruptions caused by the other representatives were even more severe.

Yes. That. To think that Saint Delyn’s Doctrine had to be invoked, and so soon… But I’m sure you know about it. Your colleagues like to keep things interesting, after all. Yes. That. To think that Saint Delyn’s Doctrine had to be invoked, and so soon… But I’m sure you know about it. Your colleagues like to keep things interesting, after all. House Hlaalu sure made its demands well known. I didn’t expect them to show such deep concern for the state of the ancestral tombs and ancestral worship. Or was it just an excuse to claim compensation for property damage? That seems more likely, somehow. But I don’t want to be unfair. The disruptions caused by some of the other representatives were just as severe, if not more so.

Yes. That. To think that Saint Delyn’s Doctrine had to be invoked, and so soon… But I’m sure you know about it. Your colleagues like to keep things interesting, after all. I consider the way the Telvanni representatives conducted themselves to be quite appalling, but who am I to question the wisdom of the mage lords? I’m sure there were many important reasons for all the insults hurled and the damage caused. It’s such a pity that those reasons remain unknown to me.

Yes. That. To think that Saint Delyn’s Doctrine had to be invoked, and so soon… Well, let’s just say that the representatives of all the Great Houses kept things interesting. With so many demands, challenges, and insults, it’s hard to decide who caused us the most trouble.

To put it mildly, yes. The trial involves the Temple and all the Great Houses. Such things happen, but it’s been a while since I’ve seen such heated debate on faith and ancestor worship. Many House nobles accused the Temple of negligence because of the way the ancestral remains were treated. There were some organizational failures that inflamed tensions, I’m afraid. I guess that’s on us, at least in part. The trial is on hiatus now, and that’s for the better. Saint Delyn’s Doctrine and all. With the way things are going, the trial will probably last many years.

It’s why we ended up in Molag Mar. I’m sure that the proximity of an old Hlaalu ancestral tomb plays a big part, as now it’s one of the major goals in our tomb purification and restoration process. Vivec city would have been nicer, but there is certainly no shortage of work around here. Molag Amur is mostly hostile wilderness, and Azura’s Coast is only slightly better. Outlaws, vampires, Daedric minions. I’m sure that they will all give us lots of trouble, but I welcome the challenge.

I have faith that these disruptions are only temporary. I am grateful for the assistance provided by the Order of the Keepers of the Dead. The Order has not been seen on Vvardenfell in quite some time, and there is always too much work and too few capable people to carry it out.

It is unfortunate how disruptive the trial has been. I think that some nobles have treated the Temple too harshly, voicing their concerns loudly for selfish reasons. However, sometimes our faith must be tested and our actions judged. Perhaps we can all learn something from the experience.
It’s been quite confusing. I’d be lying if I said I understood most of it. The Temple acts out of concern for the people. What do the Great Houses want from us?

Personally, I treat the trial as a distraction that’s also causing all sorts of annoying issues. Can you believe that some dragged ebony deals and Vvardenfell colonization effort into this? Also, claims on Temple’s negligence and a push for tomb restoration made by some families associated with House Hlaalu made other nobles scream all the louder about us being Imperial agents. I can see how some may be looking for opportunities there. I wish them good luck with their business, but I want to dedicate my efforts elsewhere.

Honestly, I try to keep my nose out of politics. Big waves happen in the ocean, and little fish like me can’t do anything about it but keep on swimming. You’re not a little fish, though %PCName. You make waves.

Honestly, I try to keep my nose out of politics. Big waves happen in the ocean, and little fish like me can’t do anything about it but keep on swimming. You don’t seem like a little fish, though, %PCName. You’re going to make big waves, I can tell.
Not the first time and not the last time. There is always another problem or another scandal. They come and go.

It’s been keeping us on edge. Well, not Nance, but she is special like that. It’s so crowded here. Quite different from Necrom, that’s for sure. And I’ve never seen the Vicar so overworked and impatient. I just try not to get in her way.

The trial certainly inflamed tensions between the Great Houses and the Temple. It looked bad from the very beginning. Many Redoran, Dres, and Indoril nobles took offence when they were seated in the wrong order, and several challenges were issued that day. Let's be honest. It was little more than a pretext for settling old grudges. I must admit, though, that seeing some smug Dres noble back down the moment Bolvyn Venim announced his intention to face him in a duel was immensely satisfying. Still, I'm not surprised that Archanon invoked Delyn's Doctrine. It was probably the only way to prevent things from escalating further.
Not my problem.
I was shocked that it was invoked as well.
I was shocked that it was invoked as well.
Why are you asking me about that? Wait. You don’t know? By the Three… they sent us a moron.
I’m not in the mood to give a lecture, outlander. Ask Ondar Selas, if you want to know. Maybe he will tell you.

Blessed be His name. There are many legal subtleties involved, but in short, Saint Delyn’s Doctrine allows the Archcanon to call a halt to the proceedings until a consensus on the key points can be reached through individual negotiations. This golden rule prevents conflicts from spiraling out of control during the trial. Some say that invoking Saint Delyn’s Doctrine is an act of desperation. It’s certainly not invoked often. In fact, it can’t be. Nor can it last forever. It’s always a strictly temporary measure and it’s no different here, as everyone will be preparing for the next stage of the trial. As for me, I call it prudence. Saint Delyn was a just and wise man. This Doctrine is one of his many contributions to Temple law.
It’s why the trial was halted. Ask Ondar Selas, if you want to know more. I focus on my job. I’m not an expert on the Doctrine.

You should know, however, that it is never an easy decision for an Archcanon, as it always comes at a cost. Some interpret such an act as a sign of weakness that can be exploited. The Doctrine can also never be invoked again in the same case, and all parties are aware of this. Still, history shows us that many agreements were reached only after Saint Delyn’s Doctrine was invoked. There can be no guarantee, but the Doctrine has proven to be effective.

I am glad that you have taken interest in the legal aspects of the Doctrine, %PCRank. Saint Delyn the Wise taught us that one should never lose sight of the primary goal. Unfortunately, this is not something that every Dunmer remembers. When the parties are too invested in the conflict or too focused on their personal gains, there is little chance of reaching an agreement which can be considered just. By invoking the Doctrine, the trial is put on hiatus and the parties are encouraged to engage in honest negotiations.

It is rare for an outlander who is not part of our congregation to take interest in the legal aspects of the Doctrine. Unfortunately, I have other duties, so I cannot discuss it with you at this time.
I will not discuss this with someone who broke the rules of the Tribunal Temple.

When there is a big family meeting and everyone starts bickering, the wise thing to do is to split up before it turns into a fight. They may not speak with each other for a while, but it’ll pass. Then they’ll start solving old problems instead of causing new ones. Saint Delyn knew that, blessed be His soul and name. He turned that wisdom into a Doctrine and we should all make use of it.
You’ve been expelled.
Mhm. Very funny. You've already joined.
Then I welcome you in our ranks, %PCRank. There's much work to be done.
Let me know if you change your mind.
You want to join us? We could certainly use the help. There is much which needs to be done. Census work, tomb purification and restoration. If you need work, we have it.

text: If you’re serious about joining, then prove yourself by your devotion to the Tribunal. Only Temple Novices, at a minimum, are eligible for service.
I will be blunt. We’re not looking for people like you. You don’t meet our requirements.

This is no secret, although some wish it were. Many ancestral tombs were abandoned or fell to cultists, necromancers, and worse. Nobles claim that it’s a stain on the honor of their clans and families, and some demand recompense for the damage done to their property as well. According to them, the tomb caretakers on Vvardenfell were marginalized on the Temple’s insistence, and the security provided by the Temple was pulled away to guard the Great Ghostfence. As the Keepers, we’re in the middle of all of this. I can’t say we’re being treated fairly. Personally, I think that the Temple defence was solid, and it’s more about politics than faith and doctrine.
Of course that the nobles love doing that. It makes it easier to accept their own failures. I don’t have to like it, though. And I never will.
I took it personally. I don’t think I’ve done anything wrong, but if I have, I’d like to know what exactly. Yet people don’t want to say it to my face or speak in vague terms. That’s annoying.

The truth is that the Temple didn’t force the nobles to change their ways. We encouraged certain changes for the greater good, but if the nobles truly disagreed, they could continue following the old ways. Some did. Yet somehow many more are now accusing the Temple of negligence, and I consider that grossly unfair. So now is the time of the Great Reorganization.

Nobody can deny that the Ghostfence protected Vvardenfell from many horrors, even when it ceased to be completely effective. Oh, it’s very convenient for the nobles to make their accusations now. I’m sure that Vvardenfell’s recent reorganization into an Imperial Province District, the surge of colonization, and the Great House struggles for influence had nothing to do with it. Nothing at all.

There were good reasons for the changes in the practice of ancestor worship. Every Dunmer had a solemn duty to support the Great Ghostfence. Well, it was as much an honor as a duty. One holy purpose. No honest Dunmer can believe otherwise. The Great Ghostfence became so central to the whole nation that few are even calling it by its full name. This was not a result of any formal act, but a cultural change. Driven by necessity, I might add.

You know better than most what role the Ghostfence served, so nobody needs to explain its importance to you. The stance of some Great House nobles seems to be flexible, but often in a way which I cannot condone. Given the danger posed by the Blight, I believe that the Temple was right in discouraging the old ways. It was not done by force, and the families could still follow their traditions if that was their firm belief.

The stance of some Great House nobles seems to be flexible, but often in a way which I cannot condone. Given the danger posed by the Blight, maintaining the Ghostfence is of utmost importance. I believe that the Temple was right in discouraging the old ways. It was not done by force, and the families could still follow their traditions if that was their firm belief.

After Saint Delyn’s doctrine was invoked and petty squabbles put to rest, some sort of compromise could be reached. We’ve been preparing a census of the ancestral tombs and family remains and keeping the families informed. We also plan to purify and restore tombs when we can and when doing so won’t result in damage to the family remains or clan property. The process had begun long before the Great Ghostfence was deactivated. Everything had to be done in a way which wouldn’t weaken the Great Ghostfence. Since the Blight is gone, maybe now we’ll be able to make faster progress.

We’ve been preparing a census of the ancestral tombs and family remains and keeping the families informed. We also plan to purify and restore tombs when we can and when doing so won’t result in damage to the family remains or clan property. All that has to be done in a way which won’t weaken the Great Ghostfence. It’s a long and arduous process.

I came up with the term myself. I plan to write a book about it, when I get the time. There was a flood of requests and demands concerning the status of family remains, urns and ancestral tombs. Many fake ones as well! Clearly an attempt at sabotage or some other intrigue.
Sure. I like simpler terms, like tomb purification and tomb restoration. They actually tell you what the work is about. But Ondar Selas probably knows what he is saying. He is a smart man, after all.
Is this what he calls it? I see. I’m less about grand words and more about actions. But it’s good that he cares. Not everybody does.

My child, it’s not “the Great Reorganization”. Things should just get back to how they once were. I love ALMSIVI and my ancestors with all my heart. We’ve all lost something when we turned away from the old rites. It pains me to see so many ancestral tombs abandoned and despoiled. I know that my ancestors think the same, as I speak with them often in Necrom. And I’m sure that ancestors of many good old Dunmer families would agree with us as well, even if some of them are too proud to admit it.
Oh, I don’t know. I don’t think about it this way. Maybe I just haven’t been with the Keepers long enough.

It’s why we ended up in Molag Mar. I’m sure that the proximity of an old Hlaalu ancestral tomb plays a big part, as now it’s one of the major goals in our tomb purification and restoration process. Vivec city would have been nicer, but there is certainly no shortage of work around here. Molag Amur is mostly hostile wilderness, and Azura’s Coast is only slightly better. Outlaws, vampires, Daedric minions. I’m sure that they will all give us lots of trouble, but I welcome the challenge.

That usually takes far longer than purification. Traditionally, the families were expected to maintain their tombs, but you already know that it’s far more complex than that. I’ll be honest. I’m a bit lost in the formalities involved. My family doesn’t even have a tomb, or at least I don’t know about it. Some remains of my ancestors are kept at my local temple, and I make my prayers there. But what’s important here is that the restoration effort can vary greatly in scope and difficulty. It’s determined by the agreement made between the Temple and the family.

She’s been with the Keepers for nearly a century now. I’m her assistant; I help with day-to-day tasks and take notes for her. She doesn’t seem bothered at all by the trial disputes, but I suppose preparing for your own funeral puts political concerns into perspective.

Surprisingly, they are the most varied and unpredictable of our foes. A tomb robber may be no more than a petty thief who was lured by the loot, or an expert killer who will make you sweat with every blow. I never underestimate them. I knew some people who did, and they paid a heavy price for it.

It’s rare to see members of the Order on Vvardenfell. It speaks to the significance of the trial, I suppose. They have important work to do here. We assist the Keepers in tomb purification duties, and conduct joint investigations as well, much to the dismay of the Ordinators. They would prefer to have sole authority over such matters. Even if they did, they don’t have the numbers to handle all of it.
The circumstances of the Order’s appearance in Molag Mar are unfortunate, but the Order’s work is just. We lend assistance when we can.

They’ve been stationed at Saint Veloth’s Hostel for some time. It’s good to see that the Temple has taken the concerns voiced by the Great Houses seriously. Practices related to ancestor worship are a matter of personal honor and conviction, but no one can doubt House Redoran’s sacrifices in the fight against Dagoth Ur’s minions. While we’ve been helping to contain the threat near the Ghostfence, far too many ancestral tombs in places under the Temple’s protection have been looted by the grave robbers or defiled by cultists.

Practices related to ancestor worship are a matter of personal honor and conviction, but no one can doubt House Redoran’s sacrifices in the fight against Dagoth Ur’s minions. While we’ve been helping to contain the threat near the Ghostfence, far too many ancestral tombs in places under the Temple’s protection have been looted by the grave robbers or defiled by cultists.
Unfortunately, we couldn’t fit the members of the Order here. They’re staying at Saint Veloth’s Hostel.

Trust me. We do a lot. When a census of tombs and ancestral remains needs to be conducted, it’s us Keepers who handle most of the work. When there are disputes concerning burials or ancestral testimonies, we come in. When tombs are defiled, we prepare detailed reports and oversee the investigations. And if there is corruption, we root it out. Well, the Ordinators do some of that as well. I will give them that.

Our presence on Vvardenfell is relatively limited. Some ignorant mer have interpreted this as abandonment. It is regrettable that so many share this misguided belief. They see a looted tomb or a misplaced urn and they blame the Keepers. What they do not want to see is all the record-keeping, all the investigations and all the other work which the Order does behind the scenes. It is very convenient to ignore all of it, but also lazy and unfair.

It’s not easy being an outlander working for the Keepers. They’re an insular division of the Temple, and they have a solemn, culturally important duty. Don’t expect to climb the ranks. The Keepers are glad to have extra hands during the trial disruptions, but once those resolve, you, Jilammu, and I are going to face a lot more scrutiny. It’s important to appropriately plan for your future.

text: The Keepers are a group within the Temple dedicated to the handling of the dead and maintenance of tombs. If you want to join, go talk with Firsylla up in St. Veloth’s Hostel.

Being a Keeper is both a privilege and a sacred duty. But even more importantly, it’s honest work. If everybody could say that they’re doing honest work, the world would be a much better place, I think.
M’Aiq does not want to keep the dead. M’Aiq wants the dead to be as far away from M’Aiq as possible.

What is it, %PCRank? You’re pretty new here. Do you expect to become a Rector or a Bursar soon? I’m glad to see your enthusiasm, but just so you know, it takes years of effort to rise so high. My advice always stays the same. Focus on the work at hand. And we’re doing some good work here.
Mhm. Yes. This reminds me of how long it took me to become %Rank. Perhaps even too long. It was not easy at all. Anyway, I wish you the very best.
It’s not the most important thing here. It took a lot of effort to become %Rank, but I’m happy with my position.

It’s not possible to easily replicate these rituals. However, as the Keepers, we deal with the matters concerning the dead on a daily basis and use sanctified methods to access the tombs we need.
